column1: # Every external source this pipeline reads, with the identifier it is pinned
# to. scripts/02_fetch_benchmarks.sh reads this file rather than holding URLs in
# the script, so changing a source is a config change and shows up in a diff.
# A note on the two PoseBusters rows, because the split is the awkward part of
# this dataset and the README explains it at length.
# The coordinates come from the PoseBusters authors' own Zenodo archive. That
# archive is the preprint version and holds 428 complexes. The published paper
# in Chemical Science reports on 308: during peer review the authors removed
# complexes whose ligand made crystal contacts. The 308-member list is not in
# the Zenodo archive, is not in the posebusters GitHub repository, and the RSC
# supplementary files returned 404 when I looked for them on 22 September 2026.
# The list used here is the one PoseBench ships, pinned to a commit. It was
# checked to contain exactly 308 entries and to be a strict subset of the 428 in
# the authors' archive, so every coordinate file still comes from the authors
# and only the subset selection is second-hand. That check runs every time
# 02_fetch_benchmarks.sh does, and the stage fails if it stops holding.
# checksum_source says who publishes the checksum being verified. "zenodo_api"
# means the value is fetched from the Zenodo API at run time and compared, so
# nothing here is self-attested. "none" means upstream publishes no checksum and
# 02_fetch_benchmarks.sh records what it received instead of verifying it.
